newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW--Meredith magazine ad share sets record.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW--Meredith magazine ad share sets record.

text.p: Meredith Corp's two flagship magazines now have a commanding combined market share over their peers, as measured by advertising revenues, said president and chief executive officer William Kerr.
Better Homes & Gardens and Ladies' Home Journal, the company's largest magazines, boosted their advertising share in the women's service sector to 39 percent in 1996 from 35 percent in 1995.
"We've never had that kind of strong market position. It's a record for us," Kerr said on Friday in an interview.
Kerr said the latest ranking puts Better Homes & Gardens and Ladies' Home Journal ahead of competitors Good Housekeeping, Redbook, Family Circle, McCall's and Woman's Day.
"The strengthening of earlier momentum continued throughout the full year with our big books (largest circulation magazines)," Kerr said.
The magazines' share of advertising revenue was measured by Publishers Information Bureau, an independent agency.
Kerr said Meredith's publishing business continues to be a strong performer, benefitting from softness in paper prices.
More details will be provided next Tuesday when Meredith releases its December 31 second-quarter results.
He said introduction of Family Money, with an initial circulation base of about 250,000, is on track with a debut planned for late summer of 1997.
Publishing makes up about 54 percent of the Des Moines-based media company's earnings and broadcasting about 43 percent. The balance comes from licensing.
Kerr said Meredith is forging ahead with plans for a weekly television program based on its Better Homes and Gardens magazine.

"We are optimistic about having this on the air in the fall. It would be our first real step into significant television programming," Kerr said. But he conceded that such a move, at least in fiscal 1997, would have no meaningful financial impact.
Kerr added that Meredith, which owns seven television stations, is actively looking for broadcasting acquisition opportunities.
"Ideally, we would like to have more western representation in our mix," he said. "We clearly would prefer to be in growth areas -- in the South or West, where possible."
Meredith shares were trading at 52, up 1/4.
